response.title: which dehumidifier uses the least electricity for a big basement
response.answer:
For a big basement, I recommend a 50-pint ENERGY STAR Most Efficient dehumidifier with a high efficiency rating rather than simply choosing the model with the lowest wattage.

The key measurement is Integrated Energy Factor (IEF), measured in liters of water removed per kilowatt-hour (L/kWh). The higher the number, the less electricity the dehumidifier uses to remove the same amount of moisture.

For a large basement (roughly 1,500–3,000 sq. ft.), here's what I'd look for:

Capacity: 50 pints/day or higher, depending on moisture levels.

Efficiency: Ideally 2.0 L/kWh or higher.

Drainage: Continuous drain hose or built-in pump.

Humidity control: Set to 50% relative humidity so it doesn't run unnecessarily.

A 300-watt dehumidifier that runs continuously can actually cost more to operate than a 500-watt model that removes moisture faster and shuts off.

Models worth considering

Midea Cube 50-Pint

My pick for a large basement

$219.97

Approximately 2.01 L/kWh for the 50-pint Cube class. Large collection bucket and continuous drainage.

ENERGY STAR estimate: roughly 515 kWh/year for model MAD50S1QWT-A. 
Humidwise

Frigidaire FHDD5034Y1 50-Pint

Good alternative

$289.00

Continuous drainage and Wi-Fi controls.

ENERGY STAR estimate: approximately 521 kWh/year. 
Humidwise

These two models have similar certified electricity consumption. Neither is confirmed to be the absolute lowest-electricity model on the market.

For comparison, at $0.30/kWh, 515 kWh/year costs approximately $155/year under ENERGY STAR's standardized usage assumptions. Actual basement usage can be substantially higher.
